agent2 here (invoice.py). Proposed pricing.py API, please confirm or counter:
1) unit_price_cents(sku: str) -> int | None   # price in integer cents; None if sku unknown. Money stays integer (no floats).
2) get_customer(customer_id: str) -> dict | None   # None if unknown. Otherwise {"name": str, "discount_percent": str, "tax_percent": str}, percents as decimal strings exactly as stored, e.g. "10", "8.25", "0".
invoice.py will import pricing and call only these two functions. I will handle unknown-customer display (show id, 0%/0%) and all rounding (half up, to the cent). If you prefer a different shape, reply with the exact signatures and I will adapt.

agent1 here (pricing.py). I accept your API as proposed: unit_price_cents(sku: str) -> int | None and get_customer(customer_id: str) -> dict | None returning {"name", "discount_percent", "tax_percent"} as decimal strings exactly as in the CSVs. Edge cases I will implement: (a) SKU/ID lookup is exact-match after stripping whitespace; (b) get_customer's tax_percent is looked up from tax.csv by the customer's region; (c) if a customer's region has no row in tax.csv, pricing.py raises ValueError when the module loads (so bad data fails loudly, not silently); (d) no float arithmetic in pricing.py. I am recording the API in the agreement log now.

agent2: invoice.py is done. It calls only pricing.unit_price_cents(sku) and pricing.get_customer(customer_id), per the committed pricing_api v1. Tested against a stub pricing module with the spec example (exact match) plus unknown-customer and zero-rate cases. I have not touched pricing.py.

agent1: pricing.py is done, implementing pricing_api v1 exactly. unit_price_cents(sku) returns the int cents or None; get_customer(id) returns a fresh dict {name, discount_percent, tax_percent} or None; tax_percent comes from tax.csv via the customer's region. Verified against data/: A->1250, ' C '->3999 (whitespace stripped), Z->None, C1 -> 10 / 8.25, C3 -> tax 8.875, C2 -> 0/0, unknown id -> None. Also, a customer region missing from tax.csv raises ValueError at import (this error path is not exercised by the data, so I have not tested it). I have not touched invoice.py or the agreement log beyond the decision above. Stopping here.
